topIssues.title: [agent] fix(deploy): idle runner pruner fails open — undeterminable runners pruned with --allow-active
topIssues.author: ss251
topIssues.body:
## Project / Coordination

- Project board: N/A - runner-fleet reliability defect found while independently reviewing #17544.
- Parent tracker or epic: relates to #15398 (cleanup bundle) and #17534 / #17544 (control-dir protection).
- Coordination Discussion: N/A.
- Suggested lane tag: claude-code-ss251

## Scope

`packages/deploy/runner-workspace-cleanup/bin/eliza-prune-idle-runner-workspaces.sh` **fails open on a destructive path**: when it cannot determine which systemd unit owns a runner directory, it classifies that runner as *orphaned* and prunes its `_work` tree with `--allow-active`, which deliberately disables the tool's own safety guard.

The script is explicit that a miss is not an error:

```bash
# Every stage tolerates a miss: no match means orphaned, not an error.
agent_name=""
if [[ -r "${runner_dir}.runner" ]]; then
  agent_name="$(sed -n 's/.*"agentName"...' "${runner_dir}.runner" | head -1 || true)"
fi
unit=""
if [[ -n "$agent_name" ]]; then ... fi
if [[ -z "$unit" ]]; then
  echo "prune $name — no runner unit resolves to it (orphaned)"
fi
```

Tolerating a miss is right for the case the comment is defending (a genuinely deregistered runner, #15398). The defect is that **"absent" and "unreadable/unparseable" collapse into the same branch**, and that branch deletes.

### Defect 1 — unreadable or unparseable `.runner` reads as orphaned

`[[ -r ... ]]` failing, a transient I/O error, a `.runner` being rewritten during registration or a runner self-update, or any schema change to `agentName` all yield `agent_name=""` → `unit=""` → **prune with `--allow-active` on a runner that may be mid-job**. There is no distinction between "this runner does not exist" and "I could not tell".

### Defect 2 — `grep -F` substring match can resolve the wrong unit

```bash
| sed 's/^actions\.runner\.//' | grep -F -- "$agent_name" | head -1
```

`grep -F` is an unanchored substring match, so agent `runner-1` matches unit `…runner-10` first (`head -1` over `list-units` order). The script then consults **the wrong unit's** `is-active` state: if `runner-10` happens to be inactive while `runner-1` is running a job, `runner-1` is pruned as inactive. Both halves of the guard — the active check and the orphan check — are defeated by the same mismatch.

### Why this matters now

`--allow-active` is passed on this path by design (the comment explains why the tool's host-global `pgrep` guard is the wrong scope under `ProtectProc=invisible`). That is defensible **only if** the per-runner proof above is sound. Under either defect the proof is unsound and the last safety net is gone.

Observed consequences on `eliza-robot-6` this week — live jobs losing files mid-run:

- `Type Check`, job [91356781391](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30694519256/job/91356781391) (run 30694519256, `quality-fork.yml`): died **4 s into `actions/checkout`** with `Missing file at path: /opt/actions-runners/runner-6/_work/_temp/_runner_file_commands/save_state_231cd9bf-d25a-4158-826f-06df318efd1f`; every later step including `Run typecheck` was `skipped`. The PR was never type-checked, and the red X had nothing to do with its diff.
- #17534 cites two further runs (30692175805, 30691649390) with the same signature.

#17544 removes the **blast radius** by protecting `_temp`/`_actions`/`_tool`/`_update`/`_PipelineMapping`, and it should land. It does not address the **misclassification**: after it, a live runner mistaken for orphaned still has its repository checkouts deleted mid-job. That is this issue.

Note this also falsifies an unconditional claim in `packages/deploy/runner-workspace-cleanup/README.md` ("Never interrupting a live job — two halves, both race-free").

## Required behavior

- Distinguish *absent* from *undeterminable*. Only a runner with no `.runner` at all — or one whose unit demonstrably does not exist — may be treated as orphaned.
- On an unreadable or unparseable `.runner`, **skip and count it**, do not prune. Fail closed on the destructive branch while keeping the sweep going for other runners (the `set -e` lesson from #15398 stands).
- Resolve the unit by exact match on the unit suffix, not an unanchored substring, so `runner-1` can never resolve to `runner-10`.
- Preserve current behavior for genuine orphans, and keep per-runner error isolation and the exit-code accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A runner directory whose `.runner` exists but is unreadable or unparseable is **not** pruned; it is reported and counted as undeterminable.
- [ ] A runner whose agentName is a strict prefix/substring of another runner's (`runner-1` vs `runner-10`) resolves to its own unit; a running `runner-1` is never pruned because `runner-10` is inactive.
- [ ] Genuine orphans (no `.runner`, or a unit that truly does not exist) are still pruned — the #15398 multi-orphan sweep still reports `pruned=2`.
- [ ] Both new behaviors are covered in `packages/deploy/runner-workspace-cleanup/smoke-test.sh`, driven through the **real** helper and **real** tool with only `systemctl` stubbed, matching the existing §10 pattern.
- [ ] Demonstrated red/green: with the fix reverted the new assertions fail; with it applied the whole smoke test passes. Both outputs attached.
- [ ] `README.md`'s race-freedom claim is amended to state the conditions under which it holds.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: N/A - shell/CI infrastructure with no rendered surface.
- [ ] Logs: full `smoke-test.sh` output before the fix (failing new assertions) and after (passing), plus the helper's sweep log showing the undeterminable runner skipped and the genuine orphan pruned in the same run.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, or agent behavior involved.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: the temporary runner tree after the sweep, showing the live runner's `_work` intact and the orphan's reclaimed.
- [ ] CI or local commands: `bash packages/deploy/runner-workspace-cleanup/smoke-test.sh`.

## Claim / Status Notes

I intend to claim and implement this immediately after filing; claim comment follows in the same session.

- AI provider/model: Anthropic / claude-fable-5
- Client / agent tooling: Claude Code

- Attribution status: self-reported

topIssues.author: aandreakis
topIssues.body:
## Project / Coordination

- Parent tracker or epic: N/A - standalone reliability defect found while running the contributor inventory.

## Contribution Provenance

AI assistance is self-reported provenance, not a request for hidden reasoning.
Use the exact runtime values; do not include secrets, tokens, private prompts,
session IDs, or chain-of-thought.

- AI assistance: yes
- AI provider/model: OpenAI / gpt-5.6-sol
- Client / agent tooling: Codex desktop
- Contribution skill revision: elizaOS/eliza@4b0bad53a7fd5cc0c1f0c507c849f27ebb53b1d3:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza
- Attribution status: self-reported

## Scope

The contributor inventory aborts the entire report when any one paginated GET made by `readGhPages` hits a transient transport or GitHub 5xx failure. During a real inventory on 2026-08-03, three clean attempts stopped at different issue-comment endpoints with `net/http: TLS handshake timeout`; a temporary GET-only retry wrapper then completed the same report.

Add bounded retry/backoff inside the trusted read-only adapter. Keep the command fixed to `gh api --method GET`, keep malformed successful output fail-fast, and do not retry authentication, authorization, validation, or other non-transient failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Known transient transport failures and retryable GitHub 5xx responses are retried a small, bounded number of times with bounded backoff.
- [ ] A later successful attempt returns the complete paginated result without partial output.
- [ ] Exhausted transient failures report the endpoint and attempt count, while non-transient failures fail immediately.
- [ ] Spawn errors and malformed successful JSON remain immediate failures.
- [ ] Deterministic tests cover immediate success, transient recovery, exhaustion, non-transient rejection, and the invariant that every attempt is GET-only.
- [ ] The real read-only inventory completes against `elizaOS/eliza`, and the resulting JSON is opened and manually inspected.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: N/A - CLI reliability change with no rendered UI.
- [ ] Logs: attach the pre-fix TLS failure and post-fix live inventory transcript inline.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, provider, action, or agent behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: attach the post-fix machine-readable inventory summary and manually reviewed candidate excerpt.
- [ ] CI or local commands: focused package test, package build/typecheck/lint checks, `bun run verify`, and the live `--json` inventory.

## Claim / Status Notes

Unclaimed at filing. No active product Project applies to this repository-infrastructure scope; ownership will be recorded by the required public claim comment and branch.

topIssues.title: fix(evidence): fork contributors cannot attach trusted document artifacts — text uploads mint untrusted /user-attachments/files/ URLs
topIssues.author: ss251
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`scripts/check-pr-evidence.mjs` cannot be satisfied with a **trusted document file** by a fork contributor, because the two document-capable URL shapes it trusts are both unreachable from a fork, and the gate's own self-test fixture encodes an upload shape GitHub does not actually mint for text.

This is adjacent to but distinct from #17588 (help text omits the pasted-transcript path — that path works and is what forks must fall back to) and #16991 (head binding).

## Reproduced on `develop` (`9bdcf068b`) — all three legs

**1. Text uploads mint the untrusted `/files/` path.** Uploading `17599-verification.log` through the PR comment-box uploader mints:

```
https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30640882/17599-verification.log
```

`trustedArtifact()` recognizes only `^/user-attachments/assets/<uuid>$` (plus legacy repo assets and the `pr-evidence` release path) — `/user-attachments/files/…` returns `null`, so a row citing it reports **`blank`**, the same as if nothing were attached. GitHub's uploader mints `/assets/<uuid>` for media (png/jpg/mp4/mov/webm…) and `/files/<id>/<name>` for exactly the text formats the gate's `EVIDENCE_FILE_EXTENSIONS` set names (`.log`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.jsonl`, `.csv`, `.md`, `.html`).

**2. The release path 404s for forks.** `node scripts/pr-evidence.mjs rows <pr> --row backend-logs=<local file>` tries to upload to the `pr-evidence` release and fails for non-collaborators:

```
HTTP 404: Not Found (https://uploads.github.com/repos/elizaOS/eliza/releases/363485569/assets?label=&name=17599-bun-runtime-inventory.json)
```

Release-asset upload requires push access, so the documented `attach` flow is maintainer/fleet-only.

**3. The self-test fixture asserts a shape GitHub never mints.** The in-file self-test builds:

```
- [ ] Backend logs: [backend.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001)
```

— a **text file at an `/assets/` UUID**. Real uploads of `backend.txt` mint `/files/…`, so the fixture green-lights an upload path that does not exist, which is why this gap ships silently.

## Impact

- A fork contributor can satisfy non-visual rows only by pasting inline (`hasInlineTranscriptEvidence`) or writing `N/A`. Pasting stops working exactly where attachment matters most: PR bodies cap at 65,536 characters, and complete real artifacts — full backend logs, real-LLM trajectory JSONL (`hasSubstantiveInlineTrajectory` requires complete JSON/JSONL records inline) — routinely exceed what fits. The Definition of Done says "attach complete, real evidence"; for forks the gate structurally forbids the attachment it demands.
- Observed concretely on #17599: `backend-logs` had to ship as a pasted transcript because the real `.log` upload was classed untrusted.

## Proposed fix (I am implementing this now — PR to follow in this session)

Trust the second first-party upload shape, with tighter validation than `/assets/` gets:

1. Add `USER_ATTACHMENT_FILE_PATH_RE = ^/user-attachments/files/[0-9]+/[^/]+$` to `trustedArtifact()`, accepted **only** when `extensionFromPath()` is in `EVIDENCE_FILE_EXTENSIONS` (the filename carries a real extension here, unlike the extensionless `/assets/` UUIDs — so `.zip`/binaries stay rejected).
2. `expectedArtifactKind()` maps those to `document`; the existing byte-level document checks (readable text, `NON_REAL_DOCUMENT_RE`, size floors) still run unchanged.
3. Correct the self-test fixture to use the `/files/` shape for `backend.txt` and keep a media fixture on `/assets/`; add red tests for a `/files/` URL with a disallowed extension and for the previously-blank classification.

No new origin is trusted: `/user-attachments/files/` is the same authenticated GitHub upload surface as `/user-attachments/assets/`, with server-assigned immutable ids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `backend-logs` row citing a real `github.com/user-attachments/files/<id>/<name>.log` upload passes the gate (verified against a live minted URL, not a synthetic one).
- [ ] `/user-attachments/files/` URLs with non-evidence extensions (e.g. `.zip`, `.exe`-style names) remain untrusted; media rows still demand real media.
- [ ] The self-test fixture no longer asserts text-at-`/assets/`; red tests cover the disallowed-extension and untrusted-shape cases.
- [ ] `node scripts/check-pr-evidence.mjs --self-test` (or the repo's equivalent invocation) and the script's test file pass; the gate's behavior for maintainer release uploads and pasted transcripts is unchanged.

## Evidence plan

- Logs: live minted `/files/` URL + `trustedArtifact()` REPL transcript before/after; full test run.
- Screenshots/video: N/A — validator policy change, no UI.
- Real-LLM trajectories: N/A — no model behavior.
- Domain artifact: the gate verdict diff (blank → ok) on a real fork-minted URL.

---

- AI provider/model: Anthropic / claude-fable-5
- Client / agent tooling: Claude Code
- Contribution skill revision: elizaOS/eliza@e37924817dd457f3c5cc1547531c7054336a3740:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza
- Attribution status: self-reported

— [claude-code-ss251]

topIssues.title: docs(agents): migration table points at four commands that do not exist
topIssues.author: greatcodeeer
topIssues.body:
## Scope

The "Removed Root Command Migrations" table in root `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` sends readers to four commands that do not exist. Following the guide produces `error: Script not found`.

Verified against `origin/develop` (`59b6f8b8`) by checking every documented replacement against `package.json`:

| Documented replacement | Exists at root? |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run audit:test-integrity:all` | **no** |
| `bun run audit:test-integrity:lane-coverage` | **no** |
| `bun run audit:test-integrity` | **no** |
| `bun run audit:test-integrity:self-test` | **no** |
| `bun run audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks` | yes |

```
$ bun run audit:test-integrity
error: Script not found "audit:test-integrity"

$ node -e 'const s=require("./package.json").scripts;
  console.log(Object.keys(s).filter(k=>k.startsWith("audit:test-integrity")).join(", "))'
audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks
```

The underlying tooling is gone too, so these are not simply unregistered scripts: `packages/scripts/` contains `lint-no-vi-mocks.mjs` and no `test-integrity` or `lane-coverage` counterpart. The one surviving entry maps to it:

```
"audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks": "node packages/scripts/lint-no-vi-mocks.mjs"
```

All other rows in the table check out — I verified the `--cwd` targets against their own package manifests (`packages/app` `test:e2e`, `packages/browser-extension` `test`, `packages/app-core` `voice:duet`, `packages/examples/smartglasses` `hardware:doctor` all exist). This is specifically the `test:lint*` family.

## Why this matters

`CLAUDE.md` states its own bar: "A wrong header is worse than no header," and the migration table exists precisely so a reader who knows the old command lands on the working one. Four of its five `test:lint*` rows currently land on a hard error.

The audience makes it sharper than a normal docs nit: this file is the repository guide **for agents**, and the table is the first thing an agent consults when a remembered command disappears. An agent that runs `bun run audit:test-integrity`, gets `Script not found`, and has no working alternative either invents a substitute or reports a blocked task — both worse than the table simply being accurate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `test:lint*` rows in root `CLAUDE.md` name only commands that exist, or state plainly that the check was retired with its tooling and no replacement exists.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` receives the identical edit — the repo convention is that the two files are byte-identical, and `bun run check:agents-claude` enforces it.
- [ ] Every remaining replacement in the table still resolves: root targets against root `package.json`, `--cwd <dir>` targets against that package's manifest.
- [ ] No change to any script or tooling — this is documentation matching reality.

## Evidence plan

- [ ] Screenshots / video: N/A - documentation change with no rendered surface.
- [ ] Logs: before/after resolution of every documented replacement, pasted inline.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, action, or provider behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: N/A - the resolution check output is the artifact.
- [ ] Commands: `bun run check:agents-claude`, plus the per-row resolution check above.

## Blockers

One open question for a maintainer, which decides the wording rather than blocking the work: were `test-integrity` / `lane-coverage` **retired deliberately** (so the rows should say so), or **lost accidentally** (so they want the tooling restored instead)? I can write it either way; I have assumed "retired" since the tooling is absent from `packages/scripts/`.

## Note on origin

Found while running the repo's own audits against a clean `develop` looking for a contribution — `audit:scripts`, `audit:alias-read-guard`, `audit:turbo-build-deps`, `audit:build-model`, `check:agents-claude`, `audit:scripts:inventory`, `audit:focused-tests`, and `audit:stale-js:self-test` all pass; this was the one thing that did not. Happy to take it, and equally happy for it to be closed if the table is knowingly aspirational.

AI provider/model: Anthropic / claude-opus-5
Client / agent tooling: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK)

topPRs.title: fix(i18n): restore the source catalog, purge dead keys, and wire the catalog checker into CI
topPRs.author: ss251
topPRs.body:
Closes #17605 `en.json` is the source catalog every other locale keys off — and it had drifted **705 keys behind source**, because the strict checker built to prevent exactly that (`packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs`) was invoked from **no CI lane, no package script, nothing**. `defaultValue` masked every miss for English users, which is why it rotted silently; all seven non-English locales render English for those strings and could never translate them. The reverse rot accumulated too: **469 dead keys** (referenced by no literal, no source template prefix, no allowlist entry) sat in every locale, plus one key translated in all seven locales that never existed in en and is used nowhere. ## Commit 1 — catalog repair (locale JSONs only) - **703 entries restored** to `en.json`, each value extracted **verbatim from its call site's inline `defaultValue`** (zero conflicting defaults across duplicate sites — no invented copy; byte-for-byte what English users already see). Pure line insertions: `703 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` on the file's existing formatting. - **3,741 dead lines purged** across all eight locales (the 469 dead keys everywhere they existed + the seven-locale orphan `mediagalleryview.SearchActive`). Pure line removals; every file re-parsed after edit. Each deletion is checker-derived: uncovered by literals AND source template prefixes AND the allowlist. - The 2 remaining source-missing keys (`settings.cloudOverview.localModeLabel`/`Description`) pass **runtime-conditional** defaults (ternaries on cloud-connection state). Cataloging them would freeze one branch and silently change rendered English (catalog wins over `defaultValue`), and splitting them is a `packages/ui` surface change requiring visual evidence — deliberately out of scope. They are declared, with reasons, in the new `uncatalogued` allowlist field, and the checker fails if such an entry ever outlives its call site. ## Commit 2 — make the checker wireable, then wire it The old contract (any locale missing any key = error) made the gate permanently red — presumably why it ended up wired nowhere. New contract, aligned with what CI can hold on every PR: - **Errors**: literal key missing from the source locale; unused source-locale key; orphaned translation (locale key absent from source); stale `uncatalogued` entry. - **Warnings** (errors under `--strict-translations`): non-source locales missing used keys / lagging the source catalog — translation debt stays *visible* on every run without blocking unrelated PRs. - `runI18nCheck` exported pure (no console/exit) with **10 fixture tests** covering each failure mode red and green, following the `ci-bun-version-contract` test pattern; the real-repo test asserts `ok:true` **and** that translation-gap warnings are present (a silent pass would hide the backfill the same way the unwired checker did). - Wired into `test.yml` beside the other contracts, so no new key can ship uncataloged again. ## Proof (verbatim)

No fixes applied. $ actionlint -config-file .github/actionlint.yaml .github/workflows/test.yml (exit 0) ```

topPRs.title: fix(packaging): define hermetic Linux runtime closure
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Closes #16446.

## Summary

- materialize the transitive Linux runtime closure from the current repository source instead of relying on a published npm package or a dependency-rich checkout
- package pinned Node and Bun runtimes for amd64 and arm64, verify archive checksums, reject dangling links and foreign-architecture ELF files, and preserve required native binaries
- make Snap, Debian, and Flatpak workflows fail closed on frozen-install, installed-launcher, version, architecture, offline-start, lifecycle, and health assertions
- keep the source Snap development-grade for beta/edge while deriving stable grade only for candidate/stable publication from trusted release inputs
- emit checksums, manifests, installed-runtime logs, SBOMs, and provenance attestations from the exact tested artifacts
- isolate pull-request package builds to read-only GitHub permissions; provenance attestation and release upload run only in trusted, non-PR jobs
- replace obsolete Flatpak npm-source generation with a current-source staging driver and tighten Store sandbox permissions

## Exact-head local validation

Base: `cc008ffcbbdd38604bb1fbd422a199affa6d4575`  
Head: `c9f7cc9ffe2bcdff0290e433e256eac33ad92c3b`

- rebased cleanly onto current `origin/develop`
- `bun install --ignore-scripts --frozen-lockfile`: passed; lockfile unchanged
- Snap semantic contract: passed for Bun 1.3.14, Node 24.15.0, amd64, and arm64
- original focused Linux contract set: 146/146 passed; post-amendment Snap contract: 69/69 passed with 95.95% validator line coverage
- packaging harness after the permission-boundary repair: 132 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `actionlint` on the Snap and Debian workflows, `shellcheck` on the installed-Snap smoke, targeted Biome, and `git diff --check`: passed
- full `bun run verify`: passed, including 573/573 Turbo tasks, all policy/script/realness audits, and 28/28 dist consumers
- verification-generated declaration residue was removed from the worktree; the published tree is clean

## Exact-package evidence gate

This PR remains intentionally draft while the exact-head GitHub jobs build and install the real Linux artifacts. Local structural tests are not represented as installed-package proof. The current exact-head runs are:

- [Debian amd64 + arm64 build/verification](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29888144323)
- [Snap amd64 + arm64 build/verification](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29888144271)
- [Flatpak build/verification](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29888144306)
- [packaging configuration and distribution checks](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29888144304)
- [changed-file coverage](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/29888144282)

An earlier diagnostic run is not final evidence: its Flatpak artifact succeeded, but manual inspection found that provenance recorded GitHub's synthetic PR merge SHA and that the uploaded checksum path did not match the flattened artifact. Those defects are repaired at this head. The same diagnostic cycle exposed the Snap `@types/node` closure gap and insufficient runtime-copier coverage; both are repaired and regression-tested here.

A later Snap diagnostic built and statically verified the real arm64 package, then exposed that its installed-runtime script changed into a read-only directory while retaining a relative evidence path. This head canonicalizes that evidence directory before the directory change and mutation-tests the invariant. It also removes OIDC and attestation write scopes from every pull-request build step; only the separate non-PR post-build job can attest the checksum-verified uploaded artifact.

Before ready-for-review, the exact-head job artifacts and logs will be manually inspected for architecture, checksums, manifests, SBOM/provenance, installed launcher behavior, lifecycle/uninstall behavior, offline startup, and health output. Any unsupported acceptance item will remain explicitly identified rather than inferred from structural tests.

topPRs.title: fix: never echo the external-content security envelope into chat
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
`hardenIncomingUserMessage` wraps external `content.text` in the untrusted-content security envelope in place. Every action that fell back to `message.content.text` as a query, name, or target was therefore holding the full envelope (markers + provenance header + payload), and several echoed it verbatim to the user — a live leak of the security armor into chat (tj-2dc95f75456876).

Fixes, applied repo-wide (~60 files):

- `unwrapUserMessageText` — a shared read-side seam in core that returns the payload for envelope-wrapped messages and trimmed raw text otherwise; exported from every core entrypoint
- shape-gated display helpers (`describeUserReference` / `userReferenceLogView` and per-plugin equivalents) so blob-shaped references are described, never echoed
- every `message.content.text` fallback across the action surface unwrapped; every user-visible echo clamped
- task `originalRequest` stores the unwrapped payload, not the armor
- honest routing copy for app-create/deploy asks, replacing text that implied the wrong lane
- `outbound-envelope-tripwire`: if the envelope ever reaches an outbound message again through any future path, MESSAGE_SENT reports it via `runtime.reportError` with a clamped preview — detection only, never a silent rewrite

Regression tests added at every fixed site (envelope-echo suites across app-control, cloud-apps, agent-skills, music, calendar, linear, personal-assistant, agent-orchestrator, and core), plus incoming-message-security coverage of the seam itself. All touched-package suites green; typecheck clean across the nine touched packages. Core security/feature suites re-run after the lint fixup: 119 files, 904 tests green.
